description: A Python harness for agents you have to operate: agents, workflows, skills and MCP tools as small declarations, with durable human-in-the-loop approvals, sessions, streaming, run control and one ordered event log per run. Wraps the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph rather than replacing them.
rules: The package is `agentdeck`: `pip install agentdeck`, `import agentdeck`. The project is branded AgentDeck SDK; there is no `agentdeck-sdk` package.
`Deck` is the only composition root, with two front doors onto one catalog: `Deck(agents=..., workflows=...)` and `Deck.from_project()`, which discovers them from a `.agentdeck/` directory.

AgentDeck owns configuration; the OpenAI Agents SDK and LangGraph own execution. An `Agent` compiles to an SDK agent and a `Workflow` to a LangGraph graph. Never suggest that AgentDeck runs its own agent loop or graph engine.

A tool is a plain Python function passed to `Agent(tools=[...])`; `build()` compiles it. A tool that declares an `agentdeck.Context[T]` parameter must NOT be wrapped in `@function_tool`, because the decorator would put the context parameter into the schema the model sees.

Application state reaches tools and workflow nodes through `Context[T]`: declare the type with `Deck(context=MyType)` and pass the instance per run with `deck.run(..., context=obj)`. A context cannot cross the HTTP surface — a run served through `Deck.asgi()` always receives `None`.

Human approval requires `durable = True` on the workflow, which requires a checkpointer, which requires the `[durability]` extra. A node that calls `interrupt()` re-runs from its start on resume, so interrupt nodes must be free of side effects.

Every run appends to one ordered event log. Status is folded from those events by `status_of`, never stored as a field. `type(event)` is always `Event`; switch on `event.payload` or `event.kind`, and always include a default case, because an unfamiliar kind parses as `UnknownEvent`.
Nothing is sandboxed. Tools, skills and workflow nodes are ordinary Python in the caller's process, and a model-chosen tool call is trusted by design.
Known defects are documented at /known-issues and should be honoured when giving advice — notably that `Agent(model=...)` is currently ignored, and that a tool which raises still completes the run.
